IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p231/r10.claim: Al-mulīm is someone who committed an offense that makes him deserving of blame.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.claim: Probably a shark swallowed Jonah; God saved him when he recognized his folly and glorified God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r6.anchor: probably a shark swallowed him but God saved him because he realized his folly and extolled the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r3.claim: Al-ḥūt means a large fish, such as a shark or whale, capable of swallowing a human whole.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r3.anchor: The word  وتُح signifies a large fish. A sea has large fish like sharks and whales

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r4.claim: The description blameworthy means Jonah deserved the calamity because God deemed him worthy of admonition; though his motive was pious, he acted without permission and was sternly chastised in proportion to his status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r4.anchor: since he did this without God’s permission he was chastised by God and such accountability is always commensurate to one’s status

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r5.claim: The word ‘whale’ is used in its familiar sense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r6.claim: ‘Blameworthy’ means having done something that invites blame; a poetic line illustrates the word ‘mulīm.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r6.anchor: ألام: أتى بما يلام عليه، قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r8.claim: مليم is read with an open mīm; although the expected form is ملوم from a wāw-root, this follows the pattern of أليم, as with comparable forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r8.anchor: وقرىء: وهو مليم، بفتح الميم، وقياسه ملوم

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r1.claim: The clause وهو مليم is circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r1.anchor: وهو مليم }: حال. والمليم: الذي أتى بما يلام عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r2.claim: المليم is someone who has done something blameworthy.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r2.anchor: والمليم: الذي أتى بما يلام عليه. قال:

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r3.claim: An anonymous poetic line uses مليم of someone blamed despite having no sin.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r3.anchor: وكم من مليم لم يصب بملامة

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r4.claim: ألام فلان means that he did something for which he deserves blame.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r4.anchor: يقال: ألام فلان أي: فعل ما يلام عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r5.speaker: قارئ شاذ
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r5.claim: A very anomalous reading has مليم with fatḥa on mīm, from لام يلوم; the expected form is ملوم, like مقول and مصون, since the root contains wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r5.anchor: وقرئ " مليم " بفتح الميم من لام يلوم، وهي شاذة جدا إذ كان قياسها " ملوم " لأنها من ذوات الواو كمقول ومصون.

SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r6.claim: The form may follow passive ليم على كذا; analogous forms are مشيب and مدعي, though مشوب and مدعو are expected from يشوب and يدعو.
SAMIN-DURR:37:142/r6.anchor: قيل: ولكن أخذت من ليم على كذا مبنيا للمفعول.

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r1.claim: All three Qur'anic references to Jonah's great fish use the definite article, perhaps because the familiar legend makes the allegory self-explanatory.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r1.anchor: it carries the definite article al. This may possibly be due to the fact that the legend of Jonah was and is so widely known

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r2.claim: The fish's interior symbolizes Jonah's spiritual distress at fleeing his prophetic mission and the presence of God.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r2.anchor: symbolizes the deep darkness of spiritual distress of which 21:87 speaks: the distress at having "fled like a runaway slave" from his prophetic mission

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r3.claim: Because humans are created weak, even prophets remain susceptible to human failings.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n56/r3.anchor: since "man has been created weak" (4:28), even prophets are not immune against all the failings inherent in human nature.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r1.claim: The preceding fragment says mayl can mean injustice as deviation from fairness, while ʿawl also conveys constriction and the weight of a burden on its bearer.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r1.anchor: بمعنى الجور ميلا عن الإنصاف. ولا يفوتنا مع هذا التقريب، ما في دلالة العول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses mulim as a sinner or offender, supported by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poetic use of al-mulim for the wrongdoer.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r2.anchor: قال: وهو مذنب. واستشهد بقول أمية بن أبي الصلت

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r3.claim: The root also appears as malum in singular and plural, as verbs in Yusuf and Ibrahim, as yatalawwamun, as lawmat la'im, and as al-nafs al-lawwama.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p382/r3.anchor: وجاء ملوم، مفرداً في آيات (الذرايات 54، الإسراء 29، 39) وجمعاً

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r2.claim: Qatada glosses Jonah’s description as blameworthy or having sinned.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p154#6/r2.anchor: قال معمر قال قتادة أي مسيء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r1.claim: The whale swallowed Jonah, taking him as a morsel, from the word luqma, a mouthful.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r2.claim: Aḥmad and others transmit from Ibn Masʿūd that a ship carrying Jonah stopped while others sailed; he identified himself as the runaway servant, and after three lots fell on him, he jumped into the sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r2.anchor: وفي خبر أخرجه أحمد وغيره عن ابن مسشعود أنه أتى قوما في سفينة فحملوه وعرفوه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's account explains the sea-lots: each person received an arrow, with the one whose arrow floated selected and the one whose sank cleared; Jonah's arrow floated.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r3.anchor: وكيفية اقتراعهم على ما في البحر عن ابن مسعود أنهم أخذوا لكل سهما على أن من طفا سهمه فهو

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r4.claim: Qatāda, in a report from Ibn Abī Ḥātim and others, says the whale was named Najm, raised its head about three cubits, pursued Jonah around the ship, and caught him before he reached the water when he jumped.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r4.anchor: وروي أنه لما وقف على شفير السفينة ليرمي بنفسه رأى حوتا واسمه على ما أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وجماعة عن قتادة نجم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r5.claim: Mulīm can mean entering a state of blame, doing something blameworthy, or blaming oneself; the forms respectively signal entering, becoming, or causation with an omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r5.anchor: أي داخل في الملامة على أن بناء أفعل للدخول في الشيء نحو أحرم إذا دخل الحرم أو آت بما يلام عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid gloss mulīm as a wrongdoer or sinner, conveying the overall sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r6.anchor: وما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد من تفسيره بالمسيء والمذنب فبيان لحاصل المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r7.speaker: قارئون
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r7.claim: A reading with fatḥa on the first letter makes mulīm a passive participle; although the expected form from the wāw-root is malūm, it is shaped on līma, as in mashīb and muddaʿī.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#3/r7.anchor: وقريء ( مليم ) بفتح أوله اسم مفعول وقياسه ملوم لأنه واوي يقال لمته ألومه لوما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r1.anchor: {فالتقمه الحوت} ابتلعه، {وهو مليم} آت بما يلام عليه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r2.claim: Mulīm describes one who has done something blameworthy.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r15.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r15.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says Jonah remained in the fish three days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r15.anchor: واختلفوا في مدة لبثه في بطن الحوت، فقال مقاتل بن حيان: ثلاثة أيام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r16.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r16.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Jonah remained in the fish seven days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r16.anchor: فقال مقاتل بن حيان: ثلاثة أيام. وقال عطاء: سبعة أيام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r17.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r17.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Jonah remained in the fish twenty days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r17.anchor: وقال عطاء: سبعة أيام. وقال الضحاك: عشرين يوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r18.speaker: السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r18.claim: Al-Suddī, al-Kalbī, and Muqātil ibn Sulaymān say Jonah remained in the fish forty days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r18.anchor: وقال السدي والكلبي ومقاتل بن سليمان: أربعين يوما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r19.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r19.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the fish swallowed Jonah at midmorning and cast him out that evening.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60#2/r19.anchor: وقال الشعبي: التقمه ضحى ولفظه عشية

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r7.claim: The fish swallowed Jonah like a morsel in one gulp.

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r8.claim: Mulīm may mean subject to blame, doing something blameworthy, or blaming himself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r8.anchor: داخل في الملامة، أو آت بما يلام عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r9.claim: A variant puts fatḥa on mīm and derives it from līma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r9.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح مبنيا من ليم كمشيب في مشوب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r12.claim: The whale gulped Jonah as one swallows a morsel; it is the familiar, largest whale, phrased as though there were no other whale.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r13.claim: Mulīm describes Jonah as entering a state that calls for blame.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: مترجمه
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.claim: The translator's Book of Jonah recounts Jonah's commission to Nineveh and flight by ship, a storm and lot that identify him, his being thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and his prayer after three days and nights in its belly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: قال مترجمه : نبدأ بمعونة الله وقوته بكتب نبوة يونان بن متى النبي

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.claim: When the boat stopped, its crew blamed an ill-omened passenger; lots fell to Jonah three times, and he jumped into the sea and was swallowed by the whale.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.anchor: فلما لم يصبهم العذاب ذهب يونس عليه السلام مغاضبا فركب في البحر في سفينة مع أناس

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the whale swallowed Jonah at midday and expelled him that evening; he did not spend a night inside it.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: التقمه الحوت ضحى ولفظه عشية ما بات في بطنه

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r7.claim: Qatada says the whale that swallowed Jonah was called Najm.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه قال {فالتقمه الحوت} يقال له نجم

DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.claim: Shahr b. Hawshab says God told the whale it was made Jonah’s refuge and mosque, not to consume him.
DURR-FULL:v7p126/r12.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب رضي الله عنه قال: انطلق يونس عليه السلام مغضبا فركب مع قوم في سفينة

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.claim: Hamid says the ship stalled, lots chose Jonah, and he asked to be tipped feet first into the sea; a pale-mouthed whale swallowed him, while a larger whale came after them.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.anchor: فركب مع قوم في سفينة فجعلت السفينة لا تنفذ ولا ترجع فقال بعضهم لبعض ماذا إلا لذنب بعضكم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r1.claim: Qatada reports that the fish was called Najm and carried Jonah through the Sea of Rome, then the Nile, Persia, and the Tigris.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه قال : فالتقمه الحوت يقال له : نجم ، فجرى به في بحر الروم ثم النيل

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “blameworthy” as having acted badly.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما في قوله : وهو مليم مسيئ

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r5.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the fish swallowed Jonah in the morning and expelled him in the evening, so he spent no night in its belly.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r5.anchor: عن الشعبي قال : التقمه الحوت ضحى ، ولفظه عشية ، ما بات في بطنه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r6.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r6.claim: Abu Malik says Jonah remained in the fish’s belly for forty days.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي مالك رضي الله ، عنه قال : لبث يونس عليه السلام في بطن الحوت اربعين يوما

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r7.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says Jonah remained in the fish for seven days as it toured all the seas, then the fish cast him onto the bank of the Tigris.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله ، عنه قال : لبث يونس في بطن الحوت سبعة ايام ، فطاف به البحار كلها

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r8.claim: Qatada says the fish was called Najm and Jonah remained in it for three days; he also says Jonah prayed much in ease and would have remained in the belly as a grave until the Day of Resurrection if he had not been among those who glorified God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3229#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه قال فالتقمه الحوت يقال له : نجم ، وانه لبث ثلاثا في جوفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r1.claim: Al-idḥāḍ literally means making someone slip; here it metaphorically means defeat and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r1.anchor: والإدحاض : جعل المرء داحضا ، أي زالقا غير ثابتت الرجلين وهو هنا استعارة للخسران والمغلوبية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r2.claim: Al-iltqām means swallowing; the fish was enormous, swallowed objects without biting, and was reportedly called al-bālīn in European usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r2.anchor: والالتقام : البلع . والحوت الذي التقمه : حوت عظيم يبتلع الأشياء ولا يعض بأسنانه ويقال : إنه الحوت الذي يسمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r3.claim: Al-mulīm is the active participle of alāma: Jonah did what made people blame him, making himself blameworthy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r3.anchor: والمليم : اسم فاعل من ألام ، إذا فعل ما يلومه عليه الناس لأنه جعلهم لائمين فهو ألامهم على نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r4.claim: The author locates Jonah’s drowning in the Sea of Rome, the Mediterranean, and rejects some exegetes’ claim that it was the Tigris.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p176/r4.anchor: ولم يكن بنهر دجلة كما غلط فيه بعض المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.claim: The narrative omits intervening events for concision; Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies a report that the ship stalled while other ships moved, so its crew blamed a sinner and cast lots.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.anchor: وهنا قصص محذوف إيجازا واختصارا، وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه لما حصل في السفينة وأبعدت في البحر ركدت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.claim: In Ibn Masʿūd's report, the sailors drew lots three times, each time naming Yūnus; when they resolved to throw him overboard, a sea creature watched him at every side of the ship, so he realized this was God's decree and leapt into its mouth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.anchor: فطفا سهم يونس، ففعلوا نحو هذا ثلاث مرات في كل مرة تقع القرعة عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r1.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r1.claim: Another report says the whale swallowed Yūnus only after he had fallen into the water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r1.anchor: التقمته بعد أن وقع في الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r2.claim: A report says God told the whale that He had not made Yūnus its food, but had made its belly a shelter and prison for him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r2.anchor: وروي أن الله أوحى إلى الحوت أني لم أجعل يونس لك رزقا وإنما جعلت بطنك له حرزا وسجنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.claim: One group says Yūnus was rescued after an hour of daylight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r3.anchor: فقالت فرقة بعد ساعة من النهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r4.claim: Another group says he was rescued after seven hours.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says Yūnus remained in the whale three days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان بعد ثلاثة أيام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says he was rescued after seven days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح بعد سبعة أيام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.claim: Another group says the period was fourteen days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة بعد أربعة عشر يوما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.speaker: أبو مالك والسدي وابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.claim: Abū Mālik and al-Suddī say forty days; Ibn Jurayj says this is what reached him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مالك والسدي بعد أربعين يوما، وهو قول ابن جريج أنه بلغه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says people embellished this story at length, so he has abridged it because the extra material is unreliable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p486#2/r2.anchor: وكثر الناس في هذا القصص بما اختصرناه لعدم الصحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r7.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r7.claim: Exegetes say God assigned a whale to swallow Jonah when he entered the water, commanded it not to harm or eat him, and the ship then sailed; iltaqamahu means it swallowed him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون وكل الله به حوتا فلما ألقى نفسه في الماء التقمه وأمر أن لا يضره ولا يكلمه وسارت السفينة حينئذ ومعنى التقمه ابتعله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says mulīm means sinful: a person is called alāma when committing a sin for which he is blamed; the cited line uses alāma in this sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p87/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة أي مذنب يقال ألام الرجل إذا أتى ذنبا يلام عليه قال الشاعر تعد معاذرا لا عذر فيها ومن يخذل أخاه فقد ألاما

BURSEVI:v7p379/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r8.claim: When selected, Jonah admitted he was the runaway and sinner, wrapped himself in his cloak, went to the bow, and threw himself into the sea.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r8.anchor: وحين خرجت القرعة على يونس قال : أنا العبد الآبق أو يا هؤلاء أنا والله العاصي فتلفف في كسائه

BURSEVI:v7p379/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r9.claim: Iltqām means swallowing a morsel; the enormous fish swallowed Jonah.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r9.anchor: فالتقمه الحوت} الإلتقام الابتلاع يعني : (لقمه كردن وفرو بردن) يقال لقمت اللقمة والتقمتها إذا ابتلعتها

BURSEVI:v7p379/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r10.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p379/r10.claim: Kashifi says God inspired a fish at the far end of the seas to open its mouth for Jonah as the ship passed.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r10.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (حق تعالى وحي فرستاد بما هي كه در آخرين ديارها باشد تايش كشتى رمده دهن بازكرده)

BURSEVI:v7p379/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r11.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p379/r11.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says a fish came from Yemen, swallowed Jonah, carried him to the lowest earth, and he heard stones glorifying God.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r11.anchor: وقال في "كشف الأسرار" : فصادفه حوت جاء من قبل اليمن فابتلعه فسفل به إلى قرار الأرضين

BURSEVI:v7p379/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r12.claim: Mulim can describe someone blamed whether deservedly or not, someone who did what merits blame, or one who blames himself.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r12.anchor: ومعنى دخوله في الملامة كونه يلام سواء استحق اللوم أم لا وأتى بما يلام عليه

BURSEVI:v7p379/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r13.claim: On the explanation that Jonah blamed himself, the hamza in alama is causative; the other explanations do not take it that way.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r13.anchor: فالهمزة على هذا للتعدية لا على التقديرين الأولين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r6.claim: God commanded a whale from the green sea to cross the seas and swallow Jonah without bruising his flesh or breaking a bone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r6.anchor: وأمر الله تعالى حوتا من البحر الأخضر أن يشق البحار، وأن يلتقم، يونس عليه السلام، فلا يهشم له لحما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r7.claim: Inside the whale Jonah thought he had died, then found himself alive, stood praying, and called the belly a place of worship no person had reached.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r7.anchor: حسب أنه قد مات ثم حرك رأسه ورجليه وأطرافه فإذا هو حي، فقام يصلي في بطن الحوت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r8.speaker: قتادة وجعفر الصادق وأبو مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r8.claim: Reports differ on Jonah's time inside the whale: Qatada says three days, Ja'far al-Sadiq a week, and Abu Malik forty days.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في مقدار ما لبث في بطن الحوت، فقيل: ثلاثة أيام، قاله قتادة. وقيل جمعة (6) قاله جعفر الصادق. وقيل: أربعين يوما، قاله أبو مالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r9.speaker: الشعبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r9.claim: Al-Sha'bi, through Mujalid, says the whale swallowed Jonah at forenoon and expelled him in the evening; Ibn Kathir says God knows the duration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r9.anchor: وقال مجالد (1) ، عن الشعبي: التقمه ضحى، وقذفه (2) عشية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r10.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r10.claim: A verse by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt says God saved Jonah by grace after he had spent nights in the belly of a fish.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r10.anchor: وفي شعر أمية بن أبي الصلت: وأنت بفضل منك نجيت يونسا … وقد بات في أضعاف حوت لياليا

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r5.claim: Iltiqām is swallowing something as a morsel.

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r6.claim: Mulīm is someone who has done something for which he is blameworthy.

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r12.claim: The clause “while he was blameworthy” is accusative as a circumstantial expression.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas relates God's order to al-lakhm, a Green Sea fish: take Jonah as prisoner, not food, and do not harm him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r3.anchor: أوحى الله تعالى إلى سمكة يقال لها اللخم من البحر الأخضر أن شقي البحار حتى تأخذي يونس , وليس يونس لك رزقا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r4.claim: God told the fish to make its belly Jonah's prison and not scratch his skin or break a bone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r4.anchor: ولكن جعلت بطنك له سجنا , فلا تخدشي له جلدا ولا تكسري له عظما

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says ملِيم means a sinner who did wrong.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r5.anchor: أي مسيء مذنب , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r6.claim: Qatada says Jonah blamed himself for what he did.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r6.anchor: يلوم نفسه على ما صنع , وهو معنى قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r7.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says Jonah was liable to blame.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r7.anchor: يلام على ما صنع , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r8.claim: مليم is one who did a blameworthy act; ملوم is one who was blamed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r8.anchor: والفرق بين الملوم والمليم أن المليم اذا أتى بما يلام عليه , والملوم إذا ليم عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.claim: Al-Sha'bi says the whale swallowed Jonah in the morning and released him that evening, after part of a day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r15.anchor: أحدها : بعض يوم , قال الشعبي : التقمه ضحى ولفظه عشية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.speaker: أبو مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r18.anchor: الرابع : أربعون يوما , قاله أبو مالك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.speaker: قيل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.claim: One report says the whale took Jonah past Eilat and returned by the Tigris to Nineveh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r19.anchor: وقيل إنه سار بيونس حتى مر به إلى الإيلة ثم عاد في دجلة إلى نينوى

MUJAHID:v2p545#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p545#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p545#4/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the one described as mulīm as sinful.
MUJAHID:v2p545#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وهو مليم ﴾ يعني مذنب

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r3.claim: Muqatil glosses mulim as surrendering himself to his Lord.

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r4.speaker: الفراء
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r4.claim: Al-Farra says alama means a man has deserved blame, while mulim describes him as blameworthy.
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: ألام الرجل إذا استحق اللوم وهو مليم

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r5.speaker: الفراء
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r5.claim: Al-Farra also says one may be blamed for an act one committed; Muqatil then returns to his own explanation.
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r5.anchor: وقال أيضا: وليم على أمر قد كان منه، فهو ملوم على ذلك، رجع إلى قول مقاتل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r1.anchor: فابتلعه ﴿ وهو مليم ﴾ داخل فى الملامة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#6/r2.claim: He was in a blameworthy state.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r10.claim: Mulīm is one who has done something blameworthy; malūm is simply someone blamed, deserving it or not. Mulīm can also mean blemished.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r10.anchor: أي أتى بما يلام عليه. فأما الملوم فهو الذي يلام، استحق ذلك أو لم يستحق

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r11.claim: The verb lāma can describe someone who acted and thereby made himself defective through that act.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abu Hurayra says God ordered the whale to take Yunus without injuring flesh or breaking bone; Yunus heard sea creatures’ glorification, prayed, and was rescued after angels interceded, then was cast ashore sick.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى ذكره حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه

STUDYQURAN:37:142/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r1.claim: Jonah was blameworthy because he fled Nineveh.
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r1.anchor: Jonah was blameworthy for having fled Nineveh.

STUDYQURAN:37:142/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r2.speaker: Kisāʾī, Qiṣaṣ al-anbiyāʾ
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r2.claim: Kisāʾī says the Ninevites beat Jonah as he called them to repent; after preaching for forty days, they dismissed him as mad.
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r2.anchor: he continued preaching to them for forty days, but they dismissed him as mad (Kisāʾī, Qiṣaṣal-anbiyāʾ)

STUDYQURAN:37:142/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r3.claim: After God sent Jonah to watch the expected punishment, the Ninevites repented and were spared; Jonah left angry, thinking God had no power over him.
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r3.anchor: Jonah went away in anger, and thought We had no power over him (21:87)

STUDYQURAN:37:142/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r4.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r4.claim: Some say Jonah fled because he was angry that the Ninevites escaped punishment for rejecting him.
STUDYQURAN:37:142/r4.anchor: Some say that he was angry that they were not punished for having rejected him

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r6.claim: The whale swallowed Jonah; al-Ṭabarī notes that فالتقلمه is the iftiʿāl form derived from laqm, swallowing.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r6.anchor: فابتلعه الحوت؛ وهو افتعل من اللقم

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r7.claim: Mulīm means one who has committed an act that merits blame, even if no one has yet blamed him verbally; malūm is the person verbally reproached.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r7.anchor: وهو مكتسب اللوم، يقال: قد ألام الرجل، إذا أتى ما يلام عليه من الأمر وإن لم يلم

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r8.claim: Labīd's line “غير مليم” witnesses the sense of deserving blame, while al-Ṭabarī distinguishes it from spoken reproach.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r8.anchor: سفها عذلت ولمت غير مليم … وهداك قبل اليوم غير حكيم

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r10.claim: Qatāda explains the blame as lying in Jonah's deed.

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd also glosses mulīm as sinful.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r11.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وهو مليم} [الصافات: 142] قال: " وهو مذنب، قال: والمليم: «المذنب»

TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Jonah uttered the supplication of 21:87, after which the whale cast him out at sunset.
TAB-FULL:v19p630/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {فالتقمه الحوت وهو مليم} [الصافات: 142] قال: قال {لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين} [الأنبياء: 87] «فلما قالها، قذفه الحوت

TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.claim: The Quran recounts only parts of Jonah's and his people's story in al-Ṣāffāt: his mission, departure, ship, fish, rescue, renewed mission, and their belief.
TABATABAI:37:133-148/r4.anchor: لم يتعرض القرآن الكريم إلا لطرف من قصته وقصة قومه فقد تعرض في سورة الصافات

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.claim: Jonah boarded a laden ship; to save it, the crew cast lots for someone to throw to a great fish, Jonah was selected and cast into the sea, and the fish swallowed him as the ship escaped.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.anchor: فساهموا وقارعوا فيما بينهم فأصابت يونس عليه السلام فألقوه في البحر فابتلعه الحوت ونجت السفينة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.claim: God preserved Jonah alive and well in the fish for days and nights; Jonah understood it as a trial for his action and called out in the fish's belly.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r4.anchor: حفظه حيا سويا في بطنه أياما وليالي ويونس عليه السلام يعلم أنها بلية ابتلاه الله بها

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī's biblical account names Jonah as son of Amittai and says God ordered him to preach to huge Nineveh, which took about three days to cross; Jonah fled to Tarshish by way of Jaffa and boarded a ship.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r8.anchor: مذكور باسم يوناه بن إمتاي في مواضع من العهد القديم وكذا في مواضع من العهد الجديد

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.claim: The lot falls on Jonah; he identifies himself as servant of the Lord, maker of land and sea, and says to throw him overboard; the sailors try to reach shore, then cast him in and the sea calms.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.anchor: فقال لهم أنا عبد الرب إله السماء خالق البر والبحر وأخبرهم خبره

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r3.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r3.claim: The biblical account says God sent a great fish that held Jonah three days and nights while he prayed; God released him on dry land and told him to go to Nineveh as commanded before.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r3.anchor: فبقي في بطنه ثلاثة أيام وثلاث ليال وصلى في بطنه إلى ربه واستغاث به

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r5.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r5.claim: Ḥabba al-ʿUranī reports that ʿAlī said God presented his wilayah to heaven and earth; Jonah rejected it, so God held him in the fish until he affirmed it. The author notes similar reports.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r5.anchor: عن حبة العرني قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن الله عرض ولايتي على أهل السماوات وعلى أهل الأرض

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r6.claim: Universal divine wilayah means God takes charge of the servant, who turns only to Him and wills only what He wills through servitude that ends in God's exclusive election of him.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r6.anchor: والمراد الولاية الكلية الإلهية التي هو عليه السلام أول من فتح بابها من هذه الأمة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.claim: Jonah's conduct displeased God and could not be ascribed to God's will; the trial made him acknowledge his own wrong and God's purity from willing such an act.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r7.anchor: فابتلاه الله بما ابتلاه ليعترف بظلمه على نفسه وأنه تعالى منزه عن إرادة مثله

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r8.claim: Trials of God's intimate servants are divine training that completes them and raises their rank, though some also include reproach; a proverb says trial accompanies intimacy.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r8.anchor: فالبلايا والمحن التي يبتلى بها الأولياء من التربية الإلهية التي يربيهم بها ويكملهم ويرفع درجاتهم

TABRISI:37:137-141/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:137-141/r9.claim: Iltqama means to swallow like a morsel; laqimahu, iltaqamahu, and talaqqamahu have the same sense.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r9.anchor: والالتقام ابتلاع اللقمة يقال: لقمه والتقمه

TABRISI:37:137-141/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:137-141/r10.claim: A person is mulim when he has done something blameworthy.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r10.anchor: وألام الرجل فهو مليم أتى بما يلام عليه

TABRISI:37:137-141/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r11.speaker: لبيد
TABRISI:37:137-141/r11.claim: Labid’s verse uses ghayr mulim, “not blameworthy,” to illustrate the word.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r11.anchor: قال لبيد: سفها عذلت ولمت غير مليم

TABRISI:37:142-147/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r5.anchor: أي ابتلعه. وقيل: إن الله سبحانه

TABRISI:37:142-147/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r6.claim: God told the whale Jonah was not made its food but its guest, and forbade it to break a bone or scratch his skin.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن الله سبحانه أوحى إلى الحوت أني لم أجعل عبدي رزقا لك

TABRISI:37:142-147/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r7.claim: Jonah deserved blame as admonition, not punishment, for leaving his people without his Lord’s command.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r7.anchor: أي مستحق للوم لوم العتاب لا لوم العقاب على خروجه من بين قومه

TABRISI:37:142-147/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:142-147/r8.claim: The author’s position is that Jonah only left a recommended act; a person can be blamed for neglecting a recommendation.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r8.anchor: وعندنا أن ذلك إنما وقع منه تركا للمندوب وقد يلام الإنسان على ترك المندوب

TABRISI:37:142-147/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:37:142-147/r9.claim: Those who allow minor sins for prophets say Jonah committed a minor sin that was expiated.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r9.anchor: ومن جوز الصغيرة على الأنبياء قال: قد وقع ذلك صغيرة مكفرة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#5/r1.claim: Mulīm means sinful; a man is called alāma when he commits a sin for which he deserves blame.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#5/r1.anchor: وهو مليم} أي مذنب. يقال: ألام الرجل (2) ؛ إذا أذنب ذنبا يلام عليه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.claim: Said b. Jubayr says a whale waited open-mouthed for its Lord's command and took Jonah when he was cast from the ship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لما استهموا في السفينة جاء حوت إلى السفينة فاغرا فاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r4.claim: The Prophet reports that God told the whale to take Jonah without tearing flesh or breaking bone; no grading is stated.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r5.claim: The exegetes gloss the whale's taking him as gulping and swallowing, from the verb for swallowing a morsel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r5.anchor: وقال المفسرون في قوله: {فالتقمه الحوت}: التهمه وابتلعه (¬8). يقال لقمت اللقمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi explains alāma as doing something for which one is blameworthy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r1.anchor: يقال: ألام إذا أتى ما يلام عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the description as Jonah's surrendering himself to his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني استلام إلى ربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the word as blameworthy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r4.speaker: قتادة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r4.claim: Qatada, reporting from Ibn Abbas, glosses it as having acted badly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة عن ابن عباس: مسيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r5.speaker: إسماعيل بن أبي خالد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r5.claim: Ismail b. Abi Khalid glosses the word as sinful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r5.anchor: وقال إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: مذنب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r6.claim: The scholars of meaning say Jonah left before God's command and committed a sin that warranted corrective discipline to keep him on the path of refinement.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106#2/r6.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: كان يونس قد خرج قبل أن يأمره الله، وكان أذنب ذنبا استحق به التأديب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r4.claim: The fish swallowed Jonah, who had done something for which he could be blamed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r4.anchor: فابتلعه { الحوت وهم مليم } أتى بما يلام عليه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan explains that God instructed the fish to swallow Jonah.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r9.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى الحوت {فالتقمه} [الصافات: 142] هذا تفسير الحسن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r7.claim: A fish opened its mouth at the bow, stern, and both sides of the ship; Jonah threw himself into the sea, and the fish swallowed him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r7.anchor: فانطلق إلى صدر السفينة ليلقي نفسه في البحر، فإذا هو بحوت فاتح فاه، فانطلق إلى ذنب السفينة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r8.claim: God told the fish not to eat or drink Jonah: He had not made Jonah its food but made its belly his prison.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r8.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى الحوت: لا تأكل عليه ولا تشرب، وقال: إني لم أجعله لك رزقا ولكني جعلت بطنك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r9.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r9.claim: Jonah remained in the fish’s belly for forty nights and called out the prayer quoted in 21:87.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r9.anchor: فمكث في بطن الحوت أربعين ليلة {فنادى في الظلمات} [الأنبياء: 87] كما قال الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r10.claim: God answered Jonah and saved him from grief in 21:88; the three darknesses are night, sea, and the fish’s belly.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r10.anchor: قال الله: {فاستجبنا له ونجيناه من الغم} [الأنبياء: 88] والظلمات: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة البحر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r11.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r11.claim: The promise that God likewise saves believers is quoted from 21:88.

ELMALILI:37:139-179/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r4.claim: The translation renders the fish swallowing Yunus while he was blameworthy.
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r4.anchor: Derken kendisini balık yuttu, melâmette idi

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.claim: The sailors tried to return to shore, then threw Yunus in; the sea calmed, a great fish swallowed him, and he remained inside for three days and nights praying.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.anchor: nihâyet Yûnus’u tuttular, gemide bulunanların necâtı için denize attılar, derhâl deniz durdu

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r14.claim: The fish immediately took Yunus as a morsel, that is, swallowed him.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r14.anchor: Derhâl balık onu lokma etti, yani yuttu

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r15.claim: Muleem describes him as blameworthy in that state, blaming himself and regretting what he had done.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r15.anchor: o hâlde ki melâmette idi, kendini levm ediyordu, pişman oluyordu

MAJAZ:v2p174/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p174/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p174/r5.claim: Alāma describes someone who did something blameworthy; Labīd’s ‘not blameworthy’ (ghayr mulīm) illustrates the word.
MAJAZ:v2p174/r5.anchor: «وهو مليم» (142) تقول العرب: ألام فلان فى أمره وذلك إذا أتى أمرا يلام عليه قال لبيد بن ربيعة:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.claim: These verses briefly report what befell Jonah after he left his homeland; the Qur’an foregrounds the story’s instructive lesson rather than supplying bare history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.anchor: Kur’an’ın amacı, salt tarihî bilgi vermek değil, olayın ibret verici yönünü öne çıkarmak olduğu için onun hayatı hakkında daha fazla ayrıntı vermeye gerek görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.speaker: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.claim: The Bible’s fuller account broadly matches the Qur’an: sent to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish, is cast overboard by lot in a storm and swallowed; after prayer he is returned ashore, recommissioned, and Nineveh repents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.anchor: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te Hz. Yûnus hakkında genel hatlarıyla Kur’an’da verilenlerle de uyuşan daha ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.claim: God used extraordinary events to train prophets for difficult struggles for monotheism; Jonah’s story illustrates that prophetic preparation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r8.anchor: Allah Teâlâ peygamberlerini, başlarına gelen olağan dışı olaylarla eğitmiş, zorlu geçecek bir tevhid mücadelesine hazırlamıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r9.claim: Jonah’s rescue from drowning through a large fish, probably a whale, was miraculous.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r9.anchor: Hz. Yûnus’un büyük bir balık, muhtemelen bir balina aracılığıyla boğulmaktan kurtulması mûcizevî bir olaydır.

NAHHAS:v3p438/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p438/r10.claim: مليم derives from ألام, doing what merits blame, unlike ملوم, one blamed whether deserving it or not.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r10.anchor: من ألام إذا أتى بما يجب أن يلام عليه مثل أحمق فهو محمق فأما الملوم فهو الذي يلام

ITQAN:v2p354/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p354/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p354/r7.claim: مليم means a sinner or wrongdoer; Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt's line calls the wrongdoer blameworthy.
ITQAN:v2p354/r7.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ وهو مليم ﴾ قال المسيء المذنب قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r1.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r1.claim: Al-Tabari distinguishes mulīm, someone who did something blameworthy whether or not blamed, from malūm, someone verbally reproached whether or not deserving it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r1.anchor: فرّق الطبري بين المليم والملوم، بأن المليم من أتى ما يلام عليه وإن لم يُلَم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r2.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says malūm is one who is blamed whether deserving or not, and reports another gloss of mulīm as blameworthy or defective.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r2.anchor: وقال القرطبي في الفرق بينهما: فأما الملوم فهو الذي يلام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r3.claim: Al-Farra explains mulīm as having committed what brings blame.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r3.anchor: ومعنى مليم عند الفراء: أتى بالائمة، وقد ألام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r4.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd that mulīm means a sinner.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r4.anchor: وأسند فيها الطبري عن مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد، أنه المذنب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r5.claim: The Qur'an's choice of the active form mulīm rather than malūm presents the person as the agent of the blameworthy cause.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p383/r5.anchor: عن ملوم إلى "مليم" يوجه إلى كونه فاعلاً لموجب اللوم
